text:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a small surge of errors from v1 clients after the v2 schema enforcement landed. Not full failures, more like soft rejects (422) on partial schema mismatches.
aj: repro? sample request/resp?
maria: pasted one from prod (sanitized):
```
POST /v2/generate
Headers: { Authorization: Bearer x, X-Redwood-Client: mysvc/1.2 }
Body: { prompt: ..., metadata: { new_field: true } }
Response 422 { error: "unknown field: metadata.new_field" }
```
aj: hm, so v2 validator is strict by default. v1 clients sending extra fields will hit that. Are we intentionally rejecting extras?
nitya: it's by design for v2 strict mode, but we should have a compatibility path. Suggestion: introduce a negotiated header `X-Redwood-Schema: v2;mode=lenient` defaulting to lenient for older clients. Telemetry flag `schema_mismatch.v1` to track.
taylor: console UX: surface a per-route "schema mismatch" card (last 24h) and a sampling of offending payloads (PII scrubbed). Also a one-click toggle to temporarily switch route to lenient fallback.
infra-bot: alert: schema_mismatch.rate for /v2/generate exceeded threshold (0.7% -> 1.9%) at 2026-03-20T14:07:20Z. Incident ID: I-20260320-21.
product-mark: If we flip lenient globally we risk hiding real bugs. Need migration window + notice to customers. Can we do a per-client policy: if client reports v1 in `X-Client-Version` treat as lenient?
aj: yes per-client fallback seems safest. Implementation idea: routing layer inspects `X-Client-Version` and `X-Redwood-Schema` then assigns validation policy. Pseudocode:
```
if client_version < 2.0:
  validation_mode = 'lenient'
elif header.schema_mode == 'lenient':
  validation_mode = 'lenient'
else:
  validation_mode = 'strict'
```
maria: good. Also want automatic telemetry tag `migration_bucket` so we can chart mismatch -> client version, region, quota tier.
console-team: mock for banner copy: "We detected schema mismatches for traffic to /v2/generate. You can enable temporary lenient validation per-client while you migrate. [Enable lenient ->]" (button opens modal to scope by client id / route / timeframe).
product-mark: add migration emails? maybe, but first step is an opt-in console toggle + API to change policy for a client.
nitya: ops note: any lenient toggle must still count quota the same and maintain audit logs. We should also tag events as `lenient_accept` vs `strict_reject`.
taylor: telemetry query I'll add to dashboards: proportion of requests with `lenient_accept` that would have failed strict validation, grouped by client_version and day. That gives migration velocity.
aj: plan: 1) deploy per-client validation switch to canary (10% of traffic) for 1 route by EOD, 2) add telemetry tags and sample payload logging, 3) add console banner + toggle. Who owns step 1?
maria: eng-runtime will pick up the switch, I'll PR today. aj can wire the routing check. taylor will add panels. console-team will do banner mock. product-mark will draft messaging.
product-mark: +1 on incremental rollout. Keep me in the loop for comms.
infra-bot: deploy started for runtime/validation-switch canary (canary id: cs-788).
maria: thanks — if we see mismatch rate drop and no regressions we'll widen to 100% in 24h.
aj: logging note: add `schema_validation.mode` and `schema_validation.result` to request spans. We need that in traces for quick triage.
nitya: i'll make sure audit trail stores the toggles and operator id.
console-team: mock ready in #design, will post links.
product-mark: action items summarized: toggle canary, telemetry tags, console banner, draft customer note. update thread when canary metrics show change. :thumbsup:
